display_title: Midpoint preservation on a quarter ball
name: MathlibAnnex.IsometryEquiv.map_midpoint_of_mem_ball
natural_language_statement: Let f:s≃ᵢt and let c∈s. Assume R>0, ball(c,R)⊆s, and ball(f(c),R)⊆t. If x,y∈s both lie in ball(c,R/4), then f sends their midpoint to the midpoint of f(x) and f(y).
one_sentence_role: Obtains a uniform local midpoint law from symmetric-lens center rigidity.

proof_steps.text: Use the triangle inequality through c to bound dist(x,y) by less than R/2.
Deduce the half-distance condition needed for a symmetric lens of radius R/2.
Show every point of the source lens lies in ball(c,R) by combining its distance to x with the R/4 bound on x.
Transport the R/4 bound from x to f(x), then prove the analogous containment of the target lens in ball(f(c),R).
Apply midpoint preservation for a set isometry whose corresponding lenses remain inside the source and target sets.

proof_summary: The two endpoints are less than R/2 apart. Their symmetric lens of radius R/2 lies in the source R-ball, and the corresponding target lens lies in the target R-ball. The subset-local lens theorem therefore applies.

source_signature.text:
theorem map_midpoint_of_mem_ball
    {s : Set E} {t : Set F} (f : s ≃ᵢ t) (c : s) {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R)
    (hsball : ball (c : E) R ⊆ s)
    (htball : ball ((f c : t) : F) R ⊆ t)
    (x y : s) (hx : (x : E) ∈ ball (c : E) (R / 4))
    (hy : (y : E) ∈ ball (c : E) (R / 4)) :
    ((f ⟨midpoint ℝ (x : E) (y : E),
          hsball (by
            rw [mem_ball]
            calc
              dist (midpoint ℝ (x : E) (y : E)) (c : E) ≤
                  (dist (x : E) (c : E) + dist (y : E) (c : E)) / 2 := by
                    simpa [dist_comm] using
                      dist_midpoint_midpoint_le (x : E) (y : E) (c : E) (c : E)
              _ < R := by rw [mem_ball] at hx hy; linarith)⟩ : t) : F) =
      midpoint ℝ ((f x : t) : F) ((f y : t) : F)
